response: Ward F/N (Matunga, Sion, Wadala) has billed Rs 9412574 of its Rs 10500000 monsoon road repair budget, or 89.6 percent, across 150 jobs. Of these, 24.7 percent were reopened within 30 days and 42.7 percent met their service deadline. Some context matters: this is a low lying ward (index 0.9) where flooding is common, and the city saw 18 days of heavy or worse rain this season. Still, Rs 2221383 was billed on DLP roads. DLP means the road is still under the original contractor's warranty, so repairs should cost the city nothing. These bills need review. Billing on 6 jobs went more than 30 percent above the rate card and should be checked. Mithi Infra Projects (synthetic) received the most spend. Example work orders include WO25-01011 and WO25-01328. Ward officers can ask: for WO25-01011, was the road under DLP, and if so, why did the city pay?
